newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Trelleborg sees 1997 earnings higher.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Trelleborg sees 1997 earnings higher.

text.p: Swedish mining and rubber group Trelleborg said on Friday that its 1997 earnings excluding possible capital gains would be higher than in 1996.

"Considering the uncertain economic trends it is difficult to give a detailed forecast but our estimate is that the full year 1997 result, excluding possible capital gains, will be better than in 1996," the company said in a statement of first quarter results.
It earlier reported a first quarter profit after financial items of 300 million crowns ($39 million), a fall of 16 percent. The market had been expecting 317 million crowns.

The profit was hurt by financial items swinging to a nine million crown charge from a 62 million crown credit in the corrresponding quarter last year due to increased debt and lower interest income, the company said in a statement.

Trelleborg did not give any debt figures but said its financial assets swung to a deficit of 1.51 billion crowns from a credit of 313 million crowns with new acquisitions accounting for 1.05 billion crowns of the charge.
Operating profit showed a 5.1 percent rise to 309 million crowns but earnings per share fell to 1.80 crowns from 2.15.
